what: acceptance-public-surfaces: an end-to-end test drives a public interface the product offers its users (its CLI, HTTP, UI, MCP or another public protocol); an integration test drives the interface of a deep module with a stable interface, public or internal, at a seam written down from the ticket's criteria before any test, never a private helper or a shallow wrapper whose interface mirrors its implementation (was: a public library function, no internal module). test-kinds: an integration test drives such a seam with stand-ins only at external boundaries; with no valid seam the implementer deepens the product code first as its own step (pin current behavior, deepen, test at the new interface), which is no test leak, while a test-only flag, hook or branch still is. Marked weakens: an integration test may now drive an internal module; the two guards are new hard requirements.
why: Owner decision 2026-11-12 on issue #795 with the director's lane brief (verbatim intent: integration tests test at 'the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside' (Matt's tdd seam) of any module, public or internal, as long as it is a deep module with a stable interface; never private helpers or shallow pass-through wrappers; mock only at external boundaries; end-to-end tests and QC/QA demos stay public surfaces only), and the owner's two relayed additions of 2026-11-12: both guards (deep module with a stable interface; seams written down up front from the ticket's criteria) are hard requirements code review blocks on, and when no valid seam exists the product code is deepened first as its own step (pin behavior, deepen, test at the new interface), which is no test leak. Amended in place 2026-11-12 before merge by owner amendment (director relay): end-to-end tests and QC/QA demos go through the product's public interfaces of any kind (CLI, HTTP, UI, MCP or another public protocol it offers its users), not CLI, HTTP or UI only.
